newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee surges to new highs on spec buying.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee surges to new highs on spec buying.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures shot to new life of contract highs across-the-board in frenzied afternoon trading as continued supply worries fueled heavy speculative buying, market sources said.
"This is out of control," one market source said. "It's wild."

The benchmark July contract hit a new life-of-contract high of 224.00 cents, a gain of 13.60 on the day, while spot spot May contract exploded to a new contract high of 255.00 cents, the highest level on a continuous weekly basis since two frosts struck Brazil in July 15, 1994.
Traders said low consumer coffee inventories and worries about the availablity of coffee for delivery against the exchange were the root of the market's sharp upswing.

Although the CSCE reported after Wednesday's close that certified coffee inventories had increased for the first time since March 31, traders said concerns about the size of exchange's stockpiles still raged.

CSCE stocks rose as of April 29 by 565 bags, but remained low at 47,668 bags -- or the equivalent of about 190 lots. Meanwhile, open interest on the May contract, which expires in less than three weeks, stood at 1,719 lots, down 414 lots as of Wednesday's close.
